concept: a lighthouse keeper's drowned wife who still climbs the stairs each night to light the lamp, and pulls anyone who follows her back down into the surf
a hermit crab the size of a wagon that wears a stolen bronze church bell as its shell and rings it by slamming its own body against the inside when it is wounded
a tar-mouthed toad the size of a cart that drags cattle into the bog
a hollow suit of tourney armor that hurls its own lance and then thunders across the field to retrieve it
a wax preacher whose sermons seal the wounds of its flock while its psalms wither the unbelievers
a clockwork bishop that blesses the poor by day and at night unfolds into a cage of brass ribs around whoever it has chosen
a brass bull construct that charges through market stalls
a stone shrine-guardian bound to the high priest it was made to protect
an adult storm dragon whose breath is a rolling wall of thunder
a mountain of troll-flesh that knits shut around the axes left in it
a gutter assassin that hides between lantern-flickers
a leopard-thing that stalks the canopy and drops on stragglers from above
a lighthouse hermit-mage whose lantern beam brands whoever it falls on, so her bolts find them again in the dark
a court astrologer who reads a foe's next move in the stars and pins them with a falling shard of light
a temple gong given legs that walks the cloister at night and strikes itself whenever it is struck
a burrowing mole-hound that hunts by tremor and surfaces beneath sleepers
a drowned bell-diver who still climbs the harbor chains at night, dragging anyone on the pier down with him
a carrion goat that eats grave-flowers and vomits a choking cloud when cornered
a glass ox forged for a tyrant's parade, hollow and humming, that charges the loudest voice in the square
a bog witch's iron cauldron that walks on three legs and cooks whatever climbs in
the drowned king's crown, a crab the size of a longboat that wears it and rules the wreck-fields
